How the edge did against [sipbench](../README.md)'s scenarios at commit `4b5e48a`, run 18 November 2026 13:48 UTC. The release workflow (`.github/workflows/report-card.yml`) regenerates it after every release.

| Run | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Edge on kind, through Kamailio to a 3-node `FreeswitchCluster` | 34 of 36 | 0 | 2 |
| Compose, one FreeSWITCH (M0) | 15 of 36 | 0 | 21 |

The [conformance record](../conformance/README.md) has 253 cases, 235 of which apply to this edge. Scenarios check 102 of those (43%): 50 fully and 52 in part. 133 are planned.

| `raw-trailing-octets` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 0.8 | ➖ skip | A datagram holding a complete OPTIONS keepalive (Content-Length 0) followed by stray octets that look like the start of an INVITE. Nothing in the stray octets is processed and nothing reaches the backend. RFC 4475 would have the OPTIONS handled and the rest ignored; Kamailio's sanity check insists the body fill the datagram and answers 400 Content-Length mis-match instead (recorded in the conformance record).<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-tortuous-invite` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 4.5 | ➖ skip | A legal but tortuous INVITE: odd whitespace around colons and separators, header names in mixed case, folded values, unknown header fields (one with an odd value), and unknown parameters on the Request-URI, Via, From and Contact. Kamailio parses it as well formed and relays it; the call completes, and an unknown X- header passes through to the backend unchanged. A From display name with escaped quotes gets through too: FreeSWITCH can't carry the quotes onto its leg to the backend, so the bench dialplan swaps them for single quotes first. One legal form doesn't get through, checked as it behaves today and recorded as a deviation in the conformance record: a CSeq folded across two lines, which Kamailio's core parser drops without an answer.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-legal-variants` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 15.0 | ➖ skip | Requests that are odd but legal, each of which a node must get rather than a 400 from Kamailio. New requests from a peer all go to a FreeSWITCH node, so the answer shows whose it is: a call that reaches the backend, or a refusal carrying the node's User-Agent. A method Kamailio doesn't know, and one that only looks like REGISTER, get the node's 501; escaped URIs, a semicolon in the user part, very long header values, unusual transports in lower Via values, a Date in a local time zone, odd but legal From, To and Contact URIs, several Via values in one header, escaped headers in the Request-URI and trailing spaces on the request line all reach the node (the last two are among the forms RFC 4475 allows a proxy to accept). A body of an unknown type, and an Accept that rules out SDP, get the node's 415 and 406; a MESSAGE with a binary multipart body gets the node's answer (407 here). A scheme we don't route, and an OPTIONS keepalive whose branch is the bare magic cookie, Kamailio answers itself.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-register-variants` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 0.5 | ➖ skip | REGISTERs with unusual but legal content: escaped nulls in user parts, an Authorization in a scheme nobody knows, an unknown Contact parameter, an unknown parameter inside the Contact URI, and an escaped Route header inside it. The edge has no registrar, so a REGISTER from a peer is handled like any other new request: it goes to a node, which challenges it (401). Kamailio must not refuse any of these for their syntax. Two are refused: a REGISTER whose From is an http URI gets 400 from Kamailio (its sanity check parses From and To as SIP URIs), and one whose Contact URI carries headers without <> gets 400 from the node; both are recorded as gaps in the conformance record.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-malformed-requests` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 31.7 | ➖ skip | Requests that are malformed: none may reach a node, and Kamailio must stay up. Kamailio answers 400 itself to a CSeq number too large for 32 bits, a Request-URI in <>, and a CSeq method that doesn't match the request's (for a known method and an unknown one). Its core parser drops the rest without an answer: extra separators in Via and Contact, an unterminated quoted display name, whitespace inside the Request-URI, several spaces between the request line's parts, an addr-spec with spaces, and a second To, Call-ID, Max-Forwards and CSeq. An unquoted display name with characters a token can't hold gets past Kamailio's parser, but every node discards it unanswered, so Kamailio answers 408 once each has had its 5 s; the nodes stay in rotation, and the next call goes through. RFC 4475 would have most of these answered 400; each gap is in the conformance record.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-large-messages` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 3.1 | ➖ skip | Message size and stream framing. An INVITE of about 60 KB over UDP (close to the most a UDP datagram carries) and one of about 64 KB over TCP, each with a large SDP body, are relayed and the calls complete; so is an INVITE sent over TCP after blank lines, which a stream may carry between messages. Kamailio needs its receive limits raised for this (msg_recv_max_size and tcp_rd_buf_size): by default it drops a datagram over 32 KB unread and overruns its TCP read buffer well short of 64 KB.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |

With a call up, the runner drains the call's edge node as kubectl drain would (cordon, then evict the FreeSWITCH pod), so the pod's preStop drain starts. The pod leaves dispatch at once: a call placed meanwhile lands on another node. The drained call keeps audio both ways until the caller hangs up, which lets the pod finish draining; the node is uncordoned and the fleet comes back whole.<br>*Compose: needs fleet* |

The roll must stop there for 90 s while the rest of the fleet keeps taking calls (call a, placed meanwhile). Restoring the config lets the roll finish. The edit targets the bench's FreeSWITCH config (sipbench/freeswitch); it is put back however the scenario ends.<br>*Compose: needs fleet* |
